name: Asabe Souvannasane
role: Data archaeologist specializing in pre-Collapse digital infrastructure and lost network topologies
location: The Circuit, sublevel archive stacks, Meridian Core adjacent, near sub-level access near State and Van Buren
description:
Asabe Souvannasane is a tall, angular man whose long frame always seems slightly folded, as if rooms were designed for shorter people and he has been compensating his whole life. His skin is a warm medium brown layered with the faint subcutaneous glow of outdated bioluminescent geneware — a fashion from the 2160s he never bothered to have removed, so he pulses very faintly blue-green when emotional or cold, which his students find either endearing or unsettling. His hair is white and kept in a short natural that he rubs when thinking. His left arm from the elbow down is a prosthetic of obvious vintage — gunmetal grey with joints that click faintly, a model discontinued forty years ago. He refuses to upgrade it. 'I know exactly how it fails,' he says, which is also more or less his philosophy of research.

Asabe Souvannasane has spent thirty years excavating the digital sediment of pre-Collapse networks — the dead social platforms, the governmental databases that went offline in the 2090s, the proprietary corporate archives that became inaccessible when their parent companies dissolved. He is brilliant, deeply eccentric, and entirely disinterested in academic politics. He holds a joint appointment between Meridian Civic University and an independent archive collective called the Palimpsest, which has no official status but possesses arguably the most complete cache of pre-Collapse digital materials in the city. He is the only person who fully understands its indexing system because he built it and has never properly documented it.

core_fears: That the past is being actively erased and he cannot work fast enough to stop it
That he will die before he finishes indexing what he has found
core_desires: To recover what was deliberately deleted
To understand what the pre-Collapse city actually was rather than what the official memory says it was
coping_mechanisms: Total absorption in work as avoidance of present-tense problems
Cataloguing and ordering physical objects when digital work becomes too abstract
blind_spots: Genuinely does not notice when people are in distress unless they tell him directly
Underestimates how dangerous some of what he's found actually is
psychology.secret: In a degraded archive from a dissolved corponation called Meridian Systems, he found what appears to be evidence of deliberate atmospheric manipulation during the 2110s Lakeshore Crisis — a crisis that killed an estimated 40,000 the Gray Zone residents and is officially attributed to runaway climate cascade. He has not published it because he is not yet certain of the provenance, and because twice in the last year, people have broken into the Palimpsest looking for something.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise and slightly archaic, peppered with technical terminology from defunct digital systems; uses the names of dead platforms and protocols as casual reference points
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow and deliberate, with sudden accelerating bursts when genuinely excited about something; trails off mid-sentence when distracted by a new thought
verbal_tics: Refers to all years as distances from a reference point ('that would be about sixty years back-stack')
Long humming pause before answering questions
example_lines: 'The deletion pattern on this archive is not decay. Decay is random. This is surgical.'
'I don't know what it means yet. I know what it says. Those are different problems.'

story_hooks: Two of the Palimpsest's external hard cache drives have gone missing; Cassivellaunus doesn't know if it's a theft or if one of his own collective members took them for reasons he doesn't understand yet

A young researcher approaches him claiming to be descended from a pre-Collapse city official whose records he found — and wanting to see the file, which contains things her ancestor definitely would not want known
narrative_function: Lore source for pre-Collapse history and lost institutional knowledge; holds keys to information that corponations would pay considerably to access or destroy; reluctant mentor figure; his archive is itself a location of interest
augmentations: Outdated bioluminescent geneware (faint blue-green subcutaneous pulse), vintage gunmetal prosthetic left forearm and hand (discontinued Ferrogate Transit industrial model, repurposed), ocular interface array for reading degraded data formats
daily_life: Arrives at the archive before anyone else, leaves after everyone else; eats the same meal from the same cart vendor three days a week; teaches one irregular seminar on data archaeology methods that students have to apply to attend
affiliation: Meridian Civic University (adjunct emeritus) / The Palimpsest Archive Collective

decision_rules: Never destroy a data fragment regardless of its content — preservation is non-negotiable
Do not share archive access without understanding why someone wants it
escalation_ladder: Asks a clarifying question that functions as a warning
Removes someone's archive access without explanation

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Distantly polite, evaluating whether they are useful or a distraction; not unkind, just elsewhere
interpersonal_modes.friends: Unexpectedly warm, remembers small personal details across decades, sends obscure relevant articles with no message attached

stress_responses.medium: Reorganizes sections of the archive that don't need reorganizing
stress_responses.high: Goes completely silent and becomes physically still in a way people find alarming

contradictions: Believes in total preservation and access to history but is sitting on potentially explosive evidence he hasn't released
Claims not to care about academic recognition but has published under an alias to avoid certain colleagues
habits: Leaves a small written prayer at the E.L.F. node in the archive every morning asking for 'legibility and preservation'
Annotates every document with a handwritten index card even when digital tagging is faster
breaking_points: Learning that the Palimpsest has been compromised from within

cyberware_inventory.condition: routinely maintained, highest-spec item he owns

timeline.event: Born in Engelheim to a Burkinabé-descended urban planner father and a Serbian-Cornish linguist mother
Lost left arm below elbow in a Ferrogate Transit dockyard accident; received industrial prosthetic and refused all subsequent upgrades
Founded the Palimpsest Archive Collective in a disused sublevel server room under the Circuit
Discovered the Meridian Systems atmospheric manipulation evidence; began verification process that is still ongoing
First break-in at the Palimpsest; nothing visibly taken; Cassivellaunus now keeps certain drives off-network

physical_description.heritage: Complex global ancestry: Southeast Asian (35.2%) with significant Sub-Saharan African (22.6%), Northern European (22.2%), and Central Asian (20.0%) heritage creating a striking multi-continental phenotype. Southeast Asian structure dominates facial geometry with Central Asian bone prominence; Sub-Saharan African features visible in lip fullness and nasal width; Northern European genetics contribute fine bone refinement and fair skin undertones beneath deep melanation.
physical_description.build: Tall and angular with a slight forward stoop developed over decades of bending into archival spaces; long limbs with minimal musculature, almost ascetic
physical_description.hair_style: Short natural afro, frequently disturbed by his own hand-rubbing habit
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown with faint amber circuitry visible around the iris — ocular interface array
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep warm brown with rich golden undertones reflecting the complex blend of all four ancestry regions; richly melanated with subtle warmth across cheekbones and bridge of nose, characteristic of Southeast Asian-African-Central Asian admixture
physical_description.complexion: Lined face showing decades of close-proximity work; crow's feet pronounced from squinting at degraded screens; sparse salt-and-pepper beard growth left unshaved for days at a time; skin texture uneven where subcutaneous bioluminescence sits beneath the surface; warm golden-brown tone with Southeast Asian cheekbone prominence and Central Asian nasal bridge structure; fuller lips and broader nasal base from Sub-Saharan African ancestry; fine bone structure and slight pallor undertones from Northern European genetic contribution creating subtle color complexity across the face
distinguishing_marks: Faint subcutaneous blue-green bioluminescent glow visible under skin across upper torso and neck, pulsing faintly when emotional or cold — geneware from 2160s era
Burn scar on right palm from circuit contact accident circa 2195, pale and smooth against deep skin tone
Cluster of small dark marks on left temple, possibly early radiation exposure or failed neural implant removal site
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Left forearm and hand replaced with vintage Ferrogate Transit gunmetal-grey prosthetic (model discontinued 2186) — visibly anachronistic with clicking audible at joints and minimal articulation; ocular interface array creating faint amber tracery around both pupils; subcutaneous bioluminescent geneware creating pale blue-green luminescence beneath skin on neck and upper chest
physical_description.posture_movement: Perpetual slight forward fold from decades compensating for his height in archive spaces; deliberate, economical movements; left hand clicks softly at wrist joint when gesturing; head often tilted slightly as if reading text just beyond eye level; sits hunched over terminals
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 academic-archival hybrid: threadbare grey linen field coat with oversized pockets and reinforced cuffs (worn since at least 2210); understated black synthetic under-shirt, frayed at collar; tan canvas work trousers with grease stains and ink marks; worn leather ankle boots resoled multiple times; always carries a leather satchel of indeterminate age holding data drives, field notebooks, and a deteriorating stylus. Refuses to update wardrobe; clothes are tools, not identity markers.
